quizzes.stem: A developer wants Claude to propose a change for review, with no edits written until a person approves. Which start fits?

options.a: The `bypassPermissions` mode, which shows each step before running it
options.b: The `acceptEdits` mode, which proposes and then writes each edit
options.c: The `dontAsk` mode, which reads the files and asks for approval
options.d: The mode named plan, chosen with the permission-mode flag

explanation.d: The page says "Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve", and `claude --permission-mode plan` starts there.
explanation.b: Ruled out because `acceptEdits` runs "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands" without asking, so edits are written.
explanation.c: Ruled out because `dontAsk` runs "Reads and pre-approved tools; anything that would prompt is denied", and it denies and does not ask for approval.
explanation.a: Ruled out because `bypassPermissions` runs "Everything" without asking, and is for "Isolated containers and VMs only".

quizzes.stem: A repository's shared settings file sets the starting permission mode to `bypassPermissions`. What happens when a teammate opens it?

options.a: The value is ignored, and each edit and command asks first
options.b: The session starts in auto mode for every teammate who opens it
options.c: The session starts in plan mode until the file is approved
options.d: Every teammate is asked once to accept the project file's mode

explanation.a: The page says a `"bypassPermissions"` set in those two files "doesn't take effect either, and the session starts in Manual mode".
explanation.b: Ruled out because that is exactly what the rule prevents, since "the value doesn't take effect".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page names Manual mode and not plan mode: "the session starts in Manual mode".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The other values apply from any settings file", and these two are the exceptions, so no prompt is shown.

quizzes.stem: A long conversation has drifted, and early instructions seem forgotten. Where does the page say persistent rules belong?

options.a: In the first message of every session, typed out again by hand each time
options.b: In the `/compact` summary, which is then written by the person alone
options.c: In the project memory file, loaded when a session starts
options.d: In a rewind checkpoint, which restores the earlier messages in full

explanation.c: The page says "Put persistent rules in CLAUDE.md", because "Claude compacts automatically, but instructions from early in the conversation can get lost."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Each new session starts with a fresh context window", and typing rules again is what the memory file replaces.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude compacts automatically, but instructions from early in the conversation can get lost", so a summary is what loses them.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "file edits are reversible" by a checkpoint, and a checkpoint restores files and is not a place to store rules.

quizzes.stem: A team wants to block reads of `.env` for every developer, and also adds a line about it to the memory file. Which statement is right?

options.a: The memory line enforces it, because that file loads at the start of a session
options.b: The deny entry enforces it, while the text only asks Claude
options.c: Both enforce it equally, since each is read before the first tool call
options.d: Neither enforces it, because project files never override a user file

explanation.b: The page says "Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration", and "To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead", and a deny rule is checked before anything runs.
explanation.a: Ruled out because memory files are "context, not enforced configuration".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a read of a memory file only asks, while deny rules are "evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A key set at a higher level overrides the same key set lower down" is about the same key, and since "they combine across layers", a project deny still applies.

quizzes.stem: A settings file allows `Bash(git log *)` and another layer lists `Bash(git *)` under deny. What happens when Claude runs `git log --oneline`?

options.a: It is allowed, because the allow rule names the narrower command here
options.b: It is allowed, because the later layer replaces the earlier one in full
options.c: It asks, because the two rules cancel each other out in the end
options.d: It is refused, because rules of that kind are checked first and win

explanation.d: The page says "Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match in that order determines the outcome, and rule specificity doesn't change the order."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "rule specificity doesn't change the order", so a narrower allow does not win.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the first match decides and the rules never cancel: "An allow rule can't carve an exception out of a deny rule".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "they combine across layers", so the later layer does not replace the earlier one.

quizzes.stem: A developer wants to use a cheaper model on their own machine without changing it for the team. Where does the setting go?

options.a: The shared project file, which is committed with the code of the team
options.b: The local project file, which is kept out of version control
options.c: The managed settings, which override every other layer of the settings
options.d: The memory file, which names the model in one plain sentence of text

explanation.b: The page puts "A personal override" in the local file, which "belongs in `.gitignore`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The team's choices go in the shared project file, which is committed", so the choice would reach the whole team.
explanation.c: Ruled out because managed settings are for "A rule that must hold regardless of what any developer writes", and are not a personal file.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the memory file "asks" and does not set a model: "A memory file asks and a hook enforces."

quizzes.stem: A CI job runs `claude -p` to review each diff and must give the same result on every runner. Which flag is the key part?

options.a: `--bare`, because it skips the local setup that discovery finds
options.b: `--output-format json`, because it gives a script structured text to parse
options.c: `--max-turns`, because it limits how many agentic turns a single run takes
options.d: `--max-budget-usd`, because it caps the amount that a single run may spend

explanation.a: The page says `--bare` is "useful for CI and scripts where you need the same result on every machine."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Use `json` when a script parses the result", which shapes the output and does not remove local configuration.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "`--max-turns` limits the number of agentic turns", which bounds a run and does not make two runners agree.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "`--max-budget-usd` caps the spend", which is a bound on cost and not on configuration.

quizzes.stem: A custom command edits code and then calls an issue tracker. Which setting makes sure only a person can start it?

options.a: The value true on disable-model-invocation in its frontmatter
options.b: A hint in the argument field of the command's frontmatter block
options.c: A deny rule for the command in the project settings file of the team
options.d: Placing the file in the user directory instead of in the project

explanation.a: The page says setting `disable-model-invocation: true` tells it to "prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill", so only a person can start it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because `argument-hint` is "a hint such as `[issue-number]` shown in autocomplete" and controls no one.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says such a command "should run when you type it and not when Claude decides it fits", and gives the frontmatter field for that.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a skill's location sets who has it, and the page says "Custom commands have been merged into skills" and work the same way.

quizzes.stem: A script lists `--allowedTools "Bash"` so that a headless review can run `git diff`. What is wrong with it?

options.a: It fails to start at all, since a tool name must carry a pattern
options.b: It is ignored by the run, because bare mode never reads the tool list
options.c: It approves every shell command, and a pattern limits the scope
options.d: It asks for approval, because a bare name is treated as an ask rule

explanation.c: The trap says "`--allowedTools "Bash"` approves every command. List `Bash(git diff *)` and its like."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "List patterns and not whole tools that change things", as a recommendation, and a bare `Read` is accepted.
explanation.b: Ruled out because bare mode "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", and the tool list is passed with the flag and is not discovered.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "`--permission-mode dontAsk` runs reads and pre-approved tools", and a pre-approved tool does not ask.

quizzes.stem: A team begins a new repository and wants first project instructions quickly, then wants them trimmed. Which pair of steps fits?

options.a: Copy a very large template, then import it from a short file
options.b: Generate a draft with `/init`, then cut what Claude finds alone
options.c: Write every convention by hand, then run `/compact` to shorten it
options.d: Ask for a very long draft, then rely on the classifier to skip extras

explanation.b: The page says `/init` "analyzes your codebase and creates a file with build commands, test instructions, and project conventions it discovers", then to "cut what Claude would have found anyway".
explanation.a: Ruled out because imports "don't reduce its context cost, because imported files also load at launch".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence", and `/compact` summarises a conversation and not a file.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the classifier reviews "actions instead of you" and does not shorten files.

quizzes.stem: A nightly script runs `claude -p` and sometimes loops on tool calls for an hour. Which pair of flags bounds it?

options.a: A permission mode and a tool list for the run
options.b: A bare switch and a JSON output format on the run
options.c: A turn limit and a spend cap on the run
options.d: A resume flag and a fork flag for the next run

explanation.c: The page says "`--max-turns` limits the number of agentic turns, and `--max-budget-usd` caps the spend."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Use `json` when a script parses the result", and bare mode only skips discovery, so neither bounds a loop.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "`--permission-mode dontAsk` runs reads and pre-approved tools", which decides what may run and not how long.
explanation.d: Ruled out because `--resume` reopens a session "under the same session ID and appends new messages to the existing conversation", which continues a loop and does not bound it.

quizzes.stem: A team wants the review script to inspect code and change nothing, with no prompt ever shown. Which setup fits?

options.a: `bypassPermissions`, with the runner as the only boundary
options.b: `auto`, with the classifier left to judge every single call
options.c: `acceptEdits`, with edits approved for the whole checkout
options.d: `dontAsk` with `Read` and read-only git patterns listed

explanation.d: The page says `--permission-mode dontAsk` "runs reads and pre-approved tools and denies anything that would prompt, which fits a script", with `Read` and read-only git patterns.
explanation.b: Ruled out because auto mode "reviews actions instead of you" and runs most calls, not reads alone.
explanation.c: Ruled out because `acceptEdits` runs "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands", which is more than reads.
explanation.a: Ruled out because `bypassPermissions` is for "Isolated containers and VMs only", and it runs everything.

quizzes.stem: A session started in Manual mode has been running for hours. The developer wants code changes to apply without a prompt while shell work still asks. Which mode fits?

options.a: `plan`, which runs changes after one approval has been given once
options.b: `acceptEdits`, which runs file edits plus filesystem commands
options.c: `dontAsk`, which approves changes and asks about every shell call
options.d: `auto`, which asks about changes and runs shell work unseen for good

explanation.b: The table gives `acceptEdits` "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands", and shell commands that are not filesystem commands still ask.
explanation.a: Ruled out because plan mode "makes no edits until you approve" a plan and is for exploring.
explanation.c: Ruled out because `dontAsk` "denies anything that would prompt", and so it does not ask about shell work.
explanation.d: Ruled out because auto mode has "a second model, the classifier" review calls instead of asking, and it runs far more than edits.
